q: What is Juxtaposition?
o: The articulation of importance by size, shape, or placement

The state of being placed close together or side-by-side, especially for comparison or contrast, used to highlight the unique qualities of individual elements by showing how they differ from their neighbors
The perception of size relative to a standard reference
The use of different elements to create visual interest and prevent monotony
n: Juxtaposition is the state of being placed close together or side-by-side, especially for comparison or contrast. In architecture, it is used to highlight the unique qualities of individual elements by showing how they differ from their neighbors.

q: Which type of artificial light provides general illumination, such as ceiling lights?
o: Natural Light
Task Light
Accent Light
Ambient Light
n: Ambient Light provides general illumination, such as ceiling lights.

q: In interior rhythm, what is Alternation (e.g., black and white tiles or striped fabric)?
o: The use of the same color across a space
A subtle, smooth flow from one space to another
Two or more elements alternating in sequence, such as black and white tiles or striped fabric
Gradual changes in elements
n: Alternation is two or more elements alternating in sequence — e.g., black and white tiles or striped fabric.

q: What is the Golden Section?
o: A 20th-century scale of proportions based on a man with an arm raised
A vernacular modular system based on a floor mat

A mathematical ratio found in nature, thought to be inherently pleasing to the human eye, expressed when a line is divided such that the ratio of the whole to the larger part is the same as the larger part to the smaller part
The ratios of a musical scale applied to the dimensions of rooms
n: The Golden Section is a mathematical ratio found in nature, thought to be inherently pleasing to the human eye. It is expressed when a line is divided such that the ratio of the whole to the larger part is the same as the larger part to the smaller part.

q: Which light temperature is described as yellowish and cozy — good for living rooms and bedrooms?
o: Natural Light
Warm Light
Ambient Light
Cool Light
n: Warm Light is yellowish and cozy — good for living rooms and bedrooms.

q: In interior design, a room's focal point (Emphasis) can be architectural or decorative. Which of the following is an example of an architectural focal point?
o: A fireplace, or a window with a view
Statement furniture
Bold artwork
A patterned area rug
n: A focal point can be architectural (e.g., a fireplace, a window with a view) or decorative (e.g., bold artwork, statement furniture).

q: What is The Modulor?
o: A mathematical ratio found in nature
A 20th-century attempt by Le Corbusier to reconcile the mathematical beauty of the Golden Section with the physical realities of the human body, based on a man with an arm raised (2.262 meters)
A vernacular modular system evolved from the size of a floor mat
The ratios of a musical scale applied to room dimensions
n: The Modulor is a 20th-century attempt to reconcile the mathematical beauty of the Golden Section with the physical realities of the human body. Le Corbusier developed a scale of proportions based on a man with an arm raised (2.262 meters), allowing for a standardized modular system applied from a chair to a city block.

q: Which colors (blue, green, purple) are calming and spacious, ideal for bedrooms and bathrooms?
o: Cool Colors
Warm Colors
Primary Colors
Neutral Colors
n: Cool Colors (blue, green, purple) are calming, spacious, and relaxing — ideal for bedrooms and bathrooms.

q: In interior design, what is Harmony?
o: The perception of size relative to a standard reference
The overall cohesion of a space despite varying elements
The juxtaposition of different elements to intensify their characteristics
A pleasing combination of elements, often achieved through a unified color palette, consistent materials, or thematic elements (e.g., Scandinavian, Industrial)
n: Harmony is a pleasing combination of elements, often achieved through a unified color palette, consistent materials, or thematic elements (e.g., Scandinavian, Industrial).

q: What is SCALE, as defined in the source material?
o: The relationship of one part to another, or to the whole
The state of equilibrium between parts of a design
The articulation of importance of a form by its size, shape, or placement
The perception of size, referring to how we perceive the size of an object in relation to a standard reference, usually the human body or the surrounding environment
n: Scale is the perception of size. It refers to how we perceive the size of an object in relation to a standard reference, usually the human body or the surrounding environment.

q: Besides setting the emotional tone of a room, what other purpose can color serve, according to the source?
o: It has no functional purpose beyond decoration
It can be used to guide focus or break up monotony
It permanently sets a room's temperature
It replaces the need for artificial or natural light
n: Use color to guide focus or break up monotony.

q: In interior design, which type of contrast is illustrated by 'a circular mirror above a rectangular console'?
o: Color contrast
Material contrast
Pattern contrast
Shape contrast
n: Shape contrast is illustrated by a circular mirror above a rectangular console.

q: Which type of architectural character refers to meaning derived from cultural or historical associations?
o: Associated Character
Functional Character
Symbolic Character
Personal Character
n: Associated Character is the meaning derived from cultural or historical associations.

q: Which texture category adds warmth and coziness (e.g., linen, rattan, brick)?
o: Rough/Matte
Tactile only
Visual only
Smooth/Glossy
n: Rough/Matte textures add warmth and coziness (e.g., linen, rattan, brick).

q: In assessing Functionality in interior design, which of the following is one of the questions the source suggests asking?
o: How many guests can the room legally hold?
Does the room match the latest social media trend?
Is there enough storage?
What is the resale value of the furniture?
n: When assessing functionality, ask: Is there enough storage? Is it easy to move around? Is lighting adequate for the activities in the space? Are the materials appropriate for the use (e.g., washable fabric in a dining area)? A room should suit its occupants' lifestyle, not just follow trends.

q: What is Positive Space in interior design?
o: The perception of an object's size
Where objects such as furniture and décor are placed
Empty areas around and between objects
A gradual change in elements
n: Positive Space is where objects (furniture, décor) are placed.

q: According to the source, where should you use cozy textures like knitted throws, and where should you use shiny textures like metal or mirrors?
o: Cozy textures in warm, sunlit rooms; shiny textures only in cooler areas
Both should be reserved exclusively for bathrooms
Neither has a recommended placement in the source
Cozy textures in cooler areas; shiny textures to reflect light in dim spaces
n: Use cozy textures (like knitted throws) in cooler areas. Use shiny textures (metal, mirrors) to reflect light in dim spaces.

q: What is Symmetrical Balance?
o: The use of dissimilar elements that have equal visual weight
Elements arranged around a central point
A gradual change in elements
Equal distribution of elements on both sides of a central axis
n: Symmetrical Balance is the equal distribution of elements on both sides of a central axis.

q: What effect do Horizontal Lines evoke in interior design (e.g., found in beds, tables, shelves)?
o: Calm, stability, and restfulness
Strength, growth, and formality
Drama and emphasis
Energy, movement, and softness
n: Horizontal Lines, found in beds, tables, and shelves, evoke calm, stability, and restfulness. They are used to widen a space.

q: Which pattern type is described as organic and flowing, feminine or traditional?
o: Abstract
Geometric
Floral
Ethnic Motifs
n: Floral patterns are organic and flowing — feminine or traditional.

q: According to Ching (2014), what is HIERARCHY?
o: The articulation of the importance of a form or space by its size, shape, or placement
The perception of size relative to a standard reference
The relationship of one part to another, or to the whole
The juxtaposition of different elements to intensify their individual characteristics
n: Ching, F. D. K. (2014), Architecture: Form, Space, and Order, defines hierarchy as the articulation of the importance of a form or space by its size, shape, or placement.

q: Dynamic Lines — diagonal, curved, or zigzag — often found in accent furniture or staircases, add what quality to a space?
o: Only structural stability
Rigidity and formality
Coldness and detachment
Playfulness, energy, movement, and softness depending on form
n: Dynamic Lines (diagonal, curved, zigzag) add energy, movement, and softness depending on form. Curves and diagonals add playfulness and are often found in accent furniture or staircases.

q: In interior design, what is the general purpose of Balance?
o: Creating movement and flow through repeated elements
Achieving a sense of equilibrium and stability in a room by distributing elements evenly, so the room doesn't feel lopsided or chaotic
Elevating a design from good to exceptional through small details
Adding drama and keeping a space visually exciting
n: Balance in interior design is about achieving a sense of equilibrium and stability in a room by distributing elements evenly. It ensures the room doesn't feel lopsided or chaotic.

q: What is UNITY in a design?
o: The three-dimensional structure of an object
The perception of size of an object relative to a standard reference
The juxtaposition of different elements to intensify their characteristics
The sense of harmony and 'oneness' in a design, where all parts belong together
n: Unity is the sense of harmony and 'oneness' in a design, where all parts belong together.

q: Which type of form is described as irregular and natural (e.g., curved chairs, oval tables), used in boho, eclectic, or nature-inspired interiors?
o: Tactile Forms
Radial Forms
Organic Forms
Geometric Forms
n: Organic Forms are irregular, natural forms (e.g., curved chairs, oval tables), used in boho, eclectic, or nature-inspired interiors.

q: In interior design principles, what is Radial Balance, and what does it create?
o: Two identical sofas facing each other — creates calm and predictability
A gradual change in wall colors
Elements arranged around a central point, such as a round dining table with equally spaced chairs or a chandelier surrounded by furniture — draws attention naturally and creates a sense of movement
A large sofa balanced by two smaller chairs — creates a casual look
n: Radial Balance arranges elements around a central point — for example, a round dining table with equally spaced chairs, or a chandelier surrounded by furniture. It draws attention naturally and creates a sense of movement.

q: What is Variety, in relation to Contrast?
o: The use of different elements to create visual interest and prevent monotony
A gradual change in elements
The state of being placed close together or side-by-side, especially for comparison
The relationship of one part to another, or to the whole
n: Variety is the use of different elements to create visual interest and prevent monotony.

q: Which quality of light comes from windows and skylights and makes spaces feel larger and more inviting?
o: Task Light
Accent Light
Natural Light
Artificial Light
n: Natural Light comes from windows and skylights. It makes spaces feel larger and more inviting.

q: In interior rhythm, what is Progression (e.g., a series of vases that increase in size)?
o: The use of the same color or pattern across a space
Two or more elements alternating in sequence
A subtle, smooth flow from one element to another
Gradual changes in elements, such as a series of vases increasing in size or a gradient of wall colors
n: Progression is gradual changes in elements — e.g., a series of vases that increase in size, or a gradient of wall colors.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three things Proportion provides, according to the source material?
o: Historically, the primary vehicle for achieving the Vitruvian ideal of Venustas (Delight)
Allows the eye to navigate the space with a sense of order
Guarantees a building will meet fire and safety codes
Different parts of a building feel like they belong to the same family
n: Proportion provides: (1) different parts of a building feel like they belong to the same family; (2) it allows the eye to navigate the space with a sense of order; and (3) historically, it has been the primary vehicle for achieving the Vitruvian ideal of Venustas (Delight).

q: Which type of artificial light is used for drama and emphasis, such as spotlights on art or under-cabinet lighting?
o: Natural Light
Ambient Light
Task Light
Accent Light
n: Accent Light is used for drama and emphasis, such as spotlights on art or under-cabinet lighting.

q: In interior design, why does every room need a focal point (Emphasis)?
o: To increase the room's storage capacity
To ensure the room follows current trends
Because it immediately draws the eye and anchors the space; without it, a room can feel bland, but too many focal points can feel chaotic
To reduce the need for artificial lighting
n: Every room needs a focal point — something that immediately draws the eye and anchors the space. All other design elements should support, and not distract from, this point. A room without emphasis can feel bland; too many focal points can feel chaotic.

q: Which Renaissance theorists believed that architecture was 'frozen music,' applying the ratios of a musical scale (consonances) to the dimensions of rooms?
o: Le Corbusier and Le Corbusier's collaborators
Andrea Palladio and Leon Battista Alberti
Vitruvius and Pevsner
Walter Gropius and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
n: Renaissance theorists like Andrea Palladio and Leon Battista Alberti believed that architecture was 'frozen music.' They applied the ratios of a musical scale (consonances) to the dimensions of rooms.

q: In interior design, which colors (red, orange, yellow) are inviting and energizing but can feel intense in large doses?
o: Warm Colors
Neutral Colors
Accent Colors
Cool Colors
n: Warm Colors (red, orange, yellow) are inviting and energizing, cozy — but can feel intense in large doses.

q: In interior design, what does Scale refer to?
o: The relationship between parts of a whole, like a lamp shade and its base
The relationship between one object's size and another's, especially in relation to the space — e.g., an oversized sectional in a small studio disrupts scale
A repeated decorative design
The emotional tone set by color
n: Scale is the relationship between one object's size and another's, especially in relation to the space. For example, an oversized sectional in a small studio disrupts scale. Scale is about spatial awareness and how furniture fits within a room.

q: What is the Ken (Japanese Modular System)?
o: A vernacular modular system that evolved from the size of a floor mat (Tatami) and the distance between columns, providing a flexible grid for standardized construction and varied spatial experiences
The application of musical ratios to room dimensions
A mathematical ratio found in nature
A 20th-century system developed by Le Corbusier
n: The Ken is a Japanese vernacular modular system that evolved from the size of a floor mat (Tatami) and the distance between columns. It provides a flexible grid that allows for both standardized construction and varied spatial experiences.

q: How many main colors should you limit your palette to for harmony, according to the source?
o: 5–6 main colors
1 color only
As many as possible
2–3 main colors
n: Limit your palette to 2–3 main colors for harmony. Light colors expand space; dark colors add depth and coziness.

q: In interior design, which type of contrast is illustrated by 'smooth leather vs. rough wood'?
o: Color contrast
Shape contrast
Pattern contrast
Material contrast
n: Material contrast is illustrated by smooth leather vs. rough wood. Without contrast, a room can feel flat; but too much contrast without unity can feel disjointed.

q: Which type of architectural character is described as 'the appearance of a building derived from its internal use'?
o: Historical Character
Associated Character
Functional Character
Personal Character
n: Functional Character is the appearance of a building derived from its internal use.

q: What is Visual Texture?
o: Texture that can be physically felt
A pattern used to energize a space
Texture that is perceived with the eyes, such as a photo of a furry blanket
The emotional tone set by a material
n: Visual Texture is perceived with the eyes (e.g., a photo of a furry blanket).

q: In interior design, what falls under 'Details' — the small decisions that elevate a design from good to exceptional?
o: The structural engineering of the building
Trim on cushions or curtains, cabinet handles, light switch plates, and stitching on upholstery
The zoning ordinances of the city
Only the overall floor plan of the room
n: Details are often overlooked, but they elevate a design from good to exceptional. This includes trim on cushions or curtains, cabinet handles, light switch plates, and stitching on upholstery.

q: In the Principles in Interior Design, what is Space (as an element)?
o: The three-dimensional structure of an object
The physical area available in a room, both the floor area and the height — it's the canvas where all other elements are placed
A repeated decorative design used to energize a space
The visual paths that guide the eye and shape the form of a room
n: Space refers to the physical area available in a room, both the floor area and the height. It's the canvas where all other elements are placed. Good space planning ensures ease of movement and accessibility.

q: Why should you mix different textures in a space, according to the source?
o: To eliminate the need for any color palette at all
To make a space feel less layered
To reduce a room's tactile qualities
To add depth — you shouldn't rely solely on color
n: Mix different textures to add depth — don't rely solely on color.

q: According to Ching (2014), what is BALANCE in architecture?
o: The relationship of one part to another or to the whole
The state of equilibrium between parts of a design, achieved through the distribution of 'visual weight' across an axis or center point
The use of dissimilar elements placed side by side
The repeated recurrence of architectural elements
n: Ching, F. D. K. (2014), Architecture: Form, Space, and Order, defines balance as the state of equilibrium between parts of a design, achieved through the distribution of 'visual weight' across an axis or center point.

q: What is Line, as an interior design element?
o: The three-dimensional structure of an object — height, width, and depth
The visual paths that guide the eye; they shape the form of everything and influence the energy of a room
A repeated decorative design used to energize and enhance a space
The surface feel or visual appearance of a material
n: Line refers to the visual paths that guide the eye. Lines shape the form of everything and influence the energy of a room.

q: Which pattern type includes squares, chevrons, and stripes, and is described as modern and structured?
o: Floral
Damask
Abstract
Geometric
n: Geometric patterns (squares, chevrons, stripes) are modern and structured.

q: According to Ching (2014), what is RHYTHM in architecture?
o: The movement characterized by a patterned recurrence of architectural elements, guiding the eye through repetition, alternation, or progression
The comparison of two or more dimensions
The state of equilibrium between parts of a design
The articulation of the importance of a form or space by its size, shape, or placement
n: Ching, F. D. K. (2014), Architecture: Form, Space, and Order, defines rhythm as the movement characterized by a patterned recurrence of architectural elements, guiding the eye through a space using repetition, alternation, or progression.

q: According to the source, what can happen if a space has too many vertical lines, or too many horizontal lines?
o: Too many verticals can feel playful; too many horizontals can feel dynamic
Too many verticals can feel rigid; too many horizontals may seem static
Both create the exact same visual effect
Neither has any effect on how a space feels
n: Too many verticals can feel rigid; too many horizontals may seem static.

q: Which pattern types are noted for adding 'character and cultural references'?
o: Abstract patterns only
Geometric and Floral only
Animal Prints, Ethnic Motifs, Damask, and Paisley
None of the pattern types add cultural references
n: Animal Prints, Ethnic Motifs, Damask, and Paisley add character and cultural references.

q: What is Emphasis, as a strategy related to hierarchy?
o: The comparison of two or more dimensions
A vernacular modular system based on a floor mat
The equal distribution of elements on both sides of a central axis
The strategy of making one element stand out among others, creating a focal point that captures attention and prevents a design from appearing flat or directionless
n: Emphasis is the strategy of making one element stand out among others. It creates a point of interest — often called a 'focal point' — that captures attention and prevents a design from appearing flat or directionless.

q: Which type of form is described as clean-edged and manmade (e.g., squares, rectangles), often used in modern and minimalist designs?
o: Geometric Forms
Tactile Forms
Organic Forms
Dynamic Forms
n: Geometric Forms are clean-edged, manmade forms (e.g., squares, rectangles), often used in modern and minimalist designs.

q: In interior design principles, what does Asymmetrical Balance look like?
o: Two identical sofas facing each other
A chandelier surrounded by furniture
A round dining table with equally spaced chairs
A large sofa balanced by two smaller chairs on the opposite side — more casual and modern, requiring a trained eye to get right, as it's more dynamic
n: Asymmetrical Balance is more casual and modern — for example, a large sofa balanced by two smaller chairs on the opposite side. It requires a trained eye to get right, as it's more dynamic.

q: What is CONTRAST in design?
o: The juxtaposition of different elements to intensify their individual characteristics, achieved through changes in color, texture, shape, or material
A mathematical ratio found in nature
The articulation of the importance of a form or space by its size, shape, or placement
The state of equilibrium between parts of a design
n: Contrast is the juxtaposition of different elements to intensify their individual characteristics. It can be achieved through changes in color, texture, shape, or material.

q: What does it mean to 'maintain form-function balance' in interior design, as illustrated by a beautiful chair?
o: Form and function can never coexist in the same object
A beautiful chair still needs to be comfortable
Function should always be prioritized over form
Form should always be prioritized over function
n: Maintaining form-function balance means, for example, that a beautiful chair still needs to be comfortable.

q: In interior rhythm, what is Repetition (e.g., blue throw pillows, a blue rug, and blue curtains)?
o: Gradual changes in elements
The use of the same color, shape, or pattern across the space
Two or more elements alternating in sequence
A subtle, smooth flow from one space to another
n: Repetition is the use of the same color, shape, or pattern across the space — e.g., blue throw pillows, a blue rug, and blue curtains.

q: PROPORTION is often described as 'The Logic of Ratios.' What does it refer to?
o: The expressive qualities of a building that allow an observer to identify its purpose
The movement characterized by a patterned recurrence of architectural elements
The relationship of one part to another, or to the whole, used to achieve Harmony, where all parts of a building appear to belong to the same family of shapes
The state of equilibrium between parts of a design
n: Proportion, 'The Logic of Ratios,' is the relationship of one part to another, or to the whole. Proportion is used to achieve Harmony, where all parts of a building appear to belong to the same family of shapes — it is inherently about the comparison of two or more dimensions.

q: Which type of artificial light is used for specific activities, such as reading lamps or kitchen lighting?
o: Task Light
Ambient Light
Accent Light
Natural Light
n: Task Light is critical for specific activities, such as reading lamps or kitchen lighting.

q: In interior rhythm, what is Transition (e.g., using an archway instead of a doorway)?
o: A subtle, smooth flow from one space or element to another, such as using an archway instead of a doorway or curved furniture
Two or more elements alternating in sequence
Gradual changes in elements
The use of the same color, shape, or pattern across a space
n: Transition is a subtle, smooth flow from one space or element to another — e.g., using an archway instead of a doorway, or curved furniture. Good rhythm creates flow and a sense of predictability and comfort.

q: In the Classical Orders, what serves as the 'Module' (basic unit) of proportion?
o: The span of the roof
The width of the pediment
The height of the entablature
The diameter of the column
n: In the Classical tradition, the diameter of the column serves as the 'Module' (basic unit) for the system of proportion.

q: Which light temperature is described as bluish and clean — great for task-heavy zones like kitchens or offices?
o: Natural Light
Accent Light
Warm Light
Cool Light
n: Cool Light is bluish and clean — great for task-heavy zones like kitchens or offices.

q: In interior design, Proportion and Scale relate to size. What ratio (about 1:1.618) is often used to achieve natural proportions, such as a lamp shade proportionate to its base?
o: The Ken
The Golden Ratio
Renaissance Musical Ratio
The Modulor
n: Proportion is the relationship between parts of a whole — for example, a lamp shade that's proportionate to the lamp base. The golden ratio (about 1:1.618) is often used to achieve natural proportions.

q: Le Corbusier's Modulor was based on a man with an arm raised, standing how tall?
o: 3.05 meters
1.618 meters
1.75 meters
2.262 meters
n: Le Corbusier developed the Modulor as a scale of proportions based on a man with an arm raised at 2.262 meters, allowing for a standardized modular system applied to everything from a chair to a city block.

q: Which colors (white, gray, beige, black) are timeless and versatile, creating balance and working with any palette?
o: Neutral Colors
Accent Colors
Cool Colors
Warm Colors
n: Neutral Colors (white, gray, beige, black) are timeless and versatile — they create balance and work with any palette.

q: In interior design, what is Unity, and why is 'variety within unity' important?
o: Unity is unrelated to harmony
Unity refers only to color matching

Unity is the overall cohesion of the space — despite varying elements, the room feels like a complete idea; variety within unity avoids a look that's too perfectly matched (and boring), while keeping a sense of order
Unity means every element must match exactly, with no variation allowed
n: Unity is the overall cohesion of the space — despite varying elements, the room feels like a complete idea. Variety within unity is important: you don't want everything to match perfectly (which can be boring), but you want a sense of order and relationship between things.

q: According to Pevsner, N. (1943) in An Outline of European Architecture, what is Architectural Character?
o: The patterned recurrence of architectural elements
The expressive qualities of a building that allow an observer to identify its purpose, origin, or the intent of the designer — the quality that makes a building look like what it is meant to be
The distribution of visual weight across an axis
The mathematical ratio of a building's proportions
n: Pevsner, N. (1943), An Outline of European Architecture, defines Character as the expressive qualities of a building that allow an observer to identify its purpose, origin, or the intent of the designer. It is the quality that makes a building look like what it is meant to be.

q: What is Tactile Texture?
o: Texture that can be physically felt, such as rough stone or smooth leather
A repeated decorative design
Texture that is perceived only with the eyes, like a photo of a furry blanket
The three-dimensional structure of an object
n: Tactile Texture can be physically felt (e.g., rough stone, smooth leather).

q: In interior design, which type of contrast is illustrated by 'black and white, light vs. dark'?
o: Pattern contrast
Color contrast
Shape contrast
Material contrast
n: Color contrast is illustrated by black and white, or light vs. dark. Contrast adds drama and keeps a space visually exciting.

q: Which type of architectural character refers to the unique style of the individual architect?
o: Functional Character
Personal Character
Associated Character
Modular Character
n: Personal Character is the unique style of the individual architect.

q: Which texture category feels modern and clean (e.g., glass, lacquered wood, tiles)?
o: Organic
Rough/Matte
Tactile only
Smooth/Glossy
n: Smooth/Glossy textures feel modern and clean (e.g., glass, lacquered wood, tiles). Shiny textures are also used to reflect light in dim spaces.

q: What are design principles in architecture?
o: Building codes that regulate construction safety
The historical timeline of architectural movements
The fundamental conceptual tools used to organize and arrange architectural elements into a cohesive and meaningful whole
A list of licensed architects and their major works
n: Design principles in architecture are the fundamental conceptual tools used to organize and arrange architectural elements into a cohesive and meaningful whole.

q: What is Negative Space in interior design, and why is it important?
o: It is where furniture is placed, and it is important for defining the color palette
It is the ceiling height of a room, important for acoustics
It is a type of dynamic line used in staircases
It is the empty area around and between objects, important for creating breathing room, avoiding clutter, and making focal points stand out
n: Negative Space is the empty area around and between objects — important for creating breathing room. Negative space helps avoid clutter and makes focal points stand out.

q: What is a Pattern, as an interior design element?
o: A repeated decorative design used to energize and enhance a space
The surface feel of a material
The three-dimensional structure of an object
The physical area available in a room
n: A pattern is a repeated decorative design used to energize and enhance a space.

q: What is Asymmetrical Balance?
o: The use of dissimilar elements that have equal visual weight
The juxtaposition of different elements to intensify their characteristics
Equal distribution of elements on both sides of a central axis
Elements arranged around a central point
n: Asymmetrical Balance is the use of dissimilar elements that have equal visual weight.

q: What do Vertical Lines (seen in doorways, curtains, tall cabinets) suggest?
o: Strength, growth, and formality
Coziness and warmth
Playfulness and energy
Calm, stability, and restfulness
n: Vertical Lines, seen in doorways, curtains, and tall cabinets, suggest strength, growth, and formality. They are used to draw the eye upward, though too many verticals can feel rigid.

q: Which pattern type is described as 'expressive and creative'?
o: Geometric
Abstract
Floral
Damask
n: Abstract patterns are expressive and creative.

q: According to Unwin, S. (2013) in Analysing Architecture, how is hierarchy further defined?
o: As the state of being placed close together for comparison
As a mathematical ratio found in nature
As the articulation of the importance or significance of a form or space by its size, shape, or placement relative to the other forms and spaces of the organization
As the sense of harmony and 'oneness' in a design
n: Unwin, S. (2013), Analysing Architecture, describes hierarchy as the articulation of the importance or significance of a form or space by its size, shape, or placement relative to the other forms and spaces of the organization.

q: What is Form, as an interior design element?
o: The three-dimensional structure of an object — height, width, and depth
The visual paths that guide the eye
The physical area available in a room
The surface feel or visual appearance of a material
n: Form is the three-dimensional structure of an object — height, width, and depth.

q: In interior design principles, what does Symmetrical Balance look like, and what does it create?
o: A large sofa balanced by two smaller chairs; creates a dynamic look
A round dining table with equally spaced chairs; creates movement
A chandelier surrounded by furniture; draws attention naturally
Two identical sofas facing each other with a coffee table in between; traditional and formal, creating calm, order, and predictability
n: Symmetrical Balance is traditional and formal — for example, two identical sofas facing each other with a coffee table in between. It creates calm, order, and predictability.

q: Complete this quote by Ching (Architecture: Form, Space, and Order): 'Unity is the state of being combined or at one... it suggests that the elements of a design are tied together by a commonality of some kind, so that they appear to belong to the ___.'
o: same family
same era
same architect
same building
n: Ching writes: 'Unity is the state of being combined or at one... it suggests that the elements of a design are tied together by a commonality of some kind, so that they appear to belong to the same family.'

q: In interior design, what does 'mixing forms' accomplish, as illustrated by a square table paired with round chairs?
o: It eliminates the need for negative space
It only works in outdoor landscaping
It always breaks form-function balance
It creates variety and can be very effective
n: Mixing forms creates variety. A square table with round chairs can be very effective.

q: In interior design, what is the general purpose of Rhythm?
o: It refers only to a room's color palette
It is the relationship between one part of a room and another
It achieves equilibrium and stability by distributing elements evenly
It guides the eye through a room and keeps the visual experience interesting
n: Rhythm guides the eye through a room and keeps the visual experience interesting.
